summary: RainCast is an open-source web dashboard that forecasts monthly precipitation for Istanbul and Izmir (2025–2030) from NASA GPM IMERG satellite data. It compares four machine-learning models against a climatology baseline and shows the expected seasonal profile, annual totals and backtest accuracy in an interactive, easy-to-use interface.
details:
RainCast is an open-source web dashboard that forecasts monthly precipitation for Istanbul and Izmir for 2025–2030, built on NASA satellite precipitation data.

How it works: We use NASA GPM IMERG Final Run, Monthly, Version 07 (GPM_3IMERGM_07, 0.1° resolution) for January 2001 – December 2024, accessed through the USF ERDDAP server and averaged over a bounding box around each city. Four machine-learning models (Random Forest, Extra Trees, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost) are trained on log-transformed precipitation using lag features (1, 2, 3 and 12 months), a 12-month rolling mean and sine/cosine seasonal terms. Forecasts are produced 72 months ahead recursively. We backtest by training on 2001–2018 and testing on 2019–2024, and compare every model against a monthly climatology baseline using RMSE.

Benefits and intended impact: The dashboard lets water managers, city planners and citizens explore the expected seasonal precipitation profile and annual totals for each city, and see how much the models actually add over a simple climatological average. Users can switch regions, toggle models and read the backtest results directly in the browser, with no installation required.

Tools: Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, XGBoost, Matplotlib), HTML/CSS/JavaScript with Chart.js, GitHub and GitHub Pages.

Creativity: Instead of presenting one model as "the" answer, we show several models side by side with an honest baseline, so users can judge reliability themselves. The whole project is a static site, so it is easy to host, reproduce and extend to other regions.

Factors we considered: data source and units, spatial averaging, avoiding data leakage by using a time-based train/test split, and transparency about limitations. Monthly precipitation is only weakly predictable far ahead and recursive forecasts tend toward the seasonal mean, so results should be read as an expected seasonal profile, not as weather forecasts.

Live demo: https://ATG55.github.io/RainCast/

Code: https://github.com/ATG55/RainCast
